unit.name: Evolution, the Themes of Biology, and Scientific Inquiry

concepts.name: Levels of Biological Organization
concepts.definition: Life is organized in a hierarchy from molecules to the biosphere.
misconceptions: Thinking ecosystem includes only living things

concepts.name: Cells: Prokaryotes vs Eukaryotes
concepts.definition: Organisms are composed of cells, which may be prokaryotic or eukaryotic.
misconceptions: Believing all cells have membrane-bound organelles

concepts.name: Genetic Information & Gene Expression
concepts.definition: DNA encodes genetic information that is used to produce RNA and protein.

concepts.name: Scientific Inquiry: Hypotheses & Theories
concepts.definition: Scientific inquiry involves forming hypotheses, testing them, and building theories.
misconceptions: Thinking a theory is a guess

concepts.name: Controlled Experiments & Variables
concepts.definition: Controlled experiments manipulate only one variable while keeping others constant.
misconceptions: Thinking sample size does not matter

question_archetypes.name: Definition Match
question_archetypes.description: Match a concept to its correct description.

question_archetypes.name: Comparison/Contrast
question_archetypes.description: Identify the property that differs between related ideas.

question_archetypes.name: Reverse Definition
question_archetypes.description: Identify an example of a concept.

question_archetypes.name: Experimental Design
question_archetypes.description: Questions about dependent variables, controls, and hypothesis testing.

question_templates.stem: Which of the following best describes a biological population?

choices.correct_pattern: A group of individuals of the same species living in the same area.
distractor_patterns: A group of different species living together.
All living and nonliving components of an area.

choices.correct_pattern: Characteristic of both prokaryotic and eukaryotic organisms.

question_templates.stem: Compared to eukaryotic cells, prokaryotic cells ______.

choices.correct_pattern: Are generally smaller and lack membrane-bound organelles.

question_templates.stem: Which organism has DNA but lacks a nuclear envelope?
The process by which a gene directs the synthesis of a protein is called ______.
How does a scientific theory differ from a hypothesis?

choices.correct_pattern: A theory is a broad explanation supported by evidence; a hypothesis is a testable, narrower statement.
distractor_patterns: Theories apply to only one observation.

question_templates.stem: In a study on nitrogen fertilizer where one group receives 0 kg/ha, which group is the control?
